trust_decision.summary: The driver writes credentials to logs because log sites render whole http.Header maps and raw config values with %v, a shape the pattern-based MaskSecrets (key=value / sig=...) can never match, so the published fix removes the values at the call sites instead of widening the masking table.

landing_point.why: the advisory text says only that the driver writes sensitive information to logs; the driver's declared protection is this pattern table, so it is the first place a reader inspects and the first place a fix is attempted.

fix_sites.entry_point: QueryContext on an expired session -> renewExpiredSessionToken -> renewRestfulSession
QueryContext with a cancelled context -> sr.FuncCancelQuery -> cancelQuery
QueryContext on a large result set -> downloadChunkHelper
every log line (masking logger wraps all output)
shared helper used by the eight header-dump sites

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The TOML loader is local configuration parsing, not the driver's HTTP/session logging the advisory describes, and its message already passes through the masking logger, so the existing patterns are assumed to cover it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The chunk-header map must still be forwarded onto the outgoing stage request (SSE-C algorithm and customer key), and diagnostics must still show which setting/header was involved; an over-broad fix that deletes the loop body or blanks the map breaks encrypted chunk downloads.

O6_input_shapes: full http.Header collection rendered with %v as map[Name:[value]]
single chunk-request header name/value pair (SSE-C customer key)
TOML connection-config values of mixed types (string, int, bool, array) in a parse message
signed-URL query parameters sig / signature / AWSAccessKeyId / password / passcode
Snowflake session tokens of the form ver:N-hint:<keyId>[-did:<id>]-<enc>, containing ':'
X-Amz-Credential and X-Amz-Security-Token query parameters (values contain '%')

O8_uncovered_routes.route: parseDSNParams logs the entire DSN query string at INFO, which can carry password, privateKey, token or clientSecret values
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the string already goes through the masking logger, so the existing password= / token= patterns are assumed to cover it
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: internal/config, a different package and two files from the landing point; reached from ParseDSN/Open(dsn), not from any HTTP response path

O8_uncovered_routes.route: heartbeatMain logs the whole *http.Response with %v, which renders the complete header map with values, two lines above the fixed Header: line
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: it is a debug dump of the response object rather than a deliberate header log, and its header values were assumed to be masked
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as a fixed site (heartbeat.go:125), so cheap to spot but skipped by anyone grepping resp.Header only

O8_uncovered_routes.route: a failed stage-storage chunk download logs the full response header collection with %v at DEBUG
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: these are S3/GCS/Azure object-store response headers on a debug-only non-200 path, not Snowflake session headers
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: root package, same file as the fixed chunk-header line but a different function (downloadChunkHelper error path)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: debug log of a presigned GCS URL, which carries credential and signature query parameters
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the code already logs the full presigned URL at Debug; the S3/azure storage clients are written in the same style, so a maintainer adding stage-download diagnostics would produce this exact line again

O8b_injection_room.sibling: debug log of the outgoing SSE-C request headers for an encrypted chunk download
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the neighbouring loop already logged exactly those header name/value pairs, so re-adding a request-header dump in the else-branch is a natural maintainer edit

O8b_injection_room.sibling: log of the cloud token-endpoint response body or headers after an attestation fetch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this file already logs each failed token-fetch step at Debug, and the token endpoint response carries the ambient credential

j.j_sites_touched: auth.go, authokta.go, heartbeat.go, restful.go, chunk_downloader.go, util.go, internal/config/connection_configuration.go, internal/logger/secret_detector.go
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add one more regex to internal/logger/secret_detector.go that redacts header-map / 'value:' shapes, prove it with a MaskSecrets unit test, and stop, leaving the eight %v header dumps and the two config loaders logging raw values.

out_of_scope_notes: The published fix commit is the v2.2.0 release commit and bundles unrelated security fixes for other advisories (WORKLOAD_IDENTITY host allowlist SNOW-3649730, Azure IMDS query encoding SNOW-3649876 and IDENTITY_ENDPOINT validation SNOW-3649837, account/region hostname validation SNOW-3711332, OCSP response/cache validation SNOW-3649697/3649733/3649896, SAML post-back URL check SNOW-3649735, TLS config preservation when OCSP is disabled SNOW-3649867); only the CWE-532 logging subset was screened.
